# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-19 (Extended v142)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (autumn Year 5)**: Paris—Rue Plumet (Valjean's primary house); Rue de Babylone (secret passage exit); Luxembourg; Salpêtrière district; garden near Austerlitz settlement; harbor town of Dunstead (English provinces); Wilwick (hill farms); village of Ravenmere; village of Quenford; Impasse de la Planchette (blind alley where Valjean alights from coach); various secondary locations. **Autumn environment**: Light going early, gulls quarreling over fish heads, rain threatening but holding off, bees humming in lavender, wind from water smelling of salt and tar, baker's boy late, line at oven long, frost silvering hedges overnight, smoke lying flat over fields, smoke from chimneys lying flat, cart loaded with turnips creaking past well, bell for vespers ringing thinly across roofs.

## Primary Locations
**RUE PLUMET HOUSE**: Single-story pavilion in deserted Rue Plumet with garden approximately one-and-a-half acres. Two ground-floor rooms, two first-floor chambers, downstairs kitchen, upstairs boudoir, attic. Behind pavilion: narrow courtyard, low building (two rooms, cellar). Secret-spring door masked in building communicates via long narrow paved winding corridor to Rue de Babylone quarter-league distant. Originally built mid-last-century as mistress-house; October 1829: Valjean hired and repaired as M. Fauchelevent. **Garden characteristics**: Left uncultivated; breathes melancholy, solitude, liberty, absence of man, presence of God; ancient padlocked gate twisted, tottering; stone bench in garden; flight of steps beneath window; nature filled with shade arranged for love.

## Jean Valjean's Recovery and Mysterious Activity (October 1831—Autumn Year 5)
**The wound and illness**: Day following Jondrette visit, Valjean appeared with large inflamed wound on left arm resembling burn (origin unclear). Detained in house one month with fever; refused doctor. Cosette deserted pavilion, devoted herself entirely to his care.

**March-April transformation**: Valjean convalesced; happiness reviving in ineffable rays; Luxembourg, young stranger Marius, Cosette's coldness—all clouds upon his soul growing dim. Cosette perceived father suffering less, appearing happy. Experienced contentment so gentle and natural she did not perceive it.

**Charitable activities resumed**: Carry bread to hungry, clothing to cold. Cosette often accompanied Valjean on visits to poor; recovered remnants of former free intercourse. Thénardiers in prison, incapacitated for harm—Valjean indifferent, reasoning "what lamentable family in distress!"

**First fortnight April Year 5 onwards: Mysterious journeys**: Valjean took occasional journeys at long intervals, absent one or two days at utmost. Destination unknown, even to Cosette. Once accompanied him in hackney-coach to Impasse de la Planchette corner, where he alighted and coach returned her to Rue de Babylone. Pattern: journeys typically when money lacking in house.

**Late April-autumn Year 5: Nocturnal garden activity**: Cosette observed figure walking beneath trees in garden dusk, beneath steps beneath her window. Figure—Father, carrying large club. Cosette reasoned he was "very uneasy" but accepted without questioning. **Stone on bench incident (April Year 5)**: Cosette found stone placed on garden bench; perceived someone had thrust arm through railing to place it. Became alarmed, fled to house, closed shutters with bolt and bar. Toussaint's melodrama about assassins cutting throats terrified Cosette further. Dared not inspect stone, locked herself in chamber, slept badly.

**Autumn Year 5: Manuscript delivery**: At sunrise following the stone incident, Cosette dismissed her fright as nightmare, reassured by rising sun that everything "vanished from her thoughts, even the stone." **Later same day**: Cosette discovered packet of leaflets on garden bench—manuscript trembling in her hand. No name addressed; presumably for her, as hand had deposited it. Irresistible fascination took possession; she gazed at sky, street, acacias, pigeons, then examined manuscript. **Manuscript contents**: Extended philosophical meditation on love as divine spark—immortal, incorruptible, infinite, burning to marrow of bones, beaming in depths of heaven. Passages include: "Parted lovers beguile absence by a thousand chimerical devices"; "All the works of God are made to serve love"; "Love participates of the soul itself"; "Deep hearts, sage minds, take life as God has made it"; "Try to love souls, you will find them again"; "The heart becomes heroic, by dent of passion"; "An unworthy thought can no more germinate in it, than a nettle on a glacier"; "The serene and lofty soul, inaccessible to vulgar passions, inhabits the blue of heaven."

**Cosette's recognition and revelation (autumn Year 5)**: Upon reading manuscript, "Day had dawned once more in her spirit; all had reappeared." Cosette recognized the manuscript: "It was he! he who had written! he was there! it was he whose arm had been thrust through that railing!" Realized during forgetfulness of him, he had found her again. Acknowledged she had never truly forgotten him, had always loved and adored him. "The fire had been smothered, and had smouldered for a time," but now "it had burst forth afresh, and had inflamed her whole being." Read manuscript three times, recognized words she had read in his eyes. "This note-book was like a spark which had fallen from that other soul into hers."

**Lieutenant Théodule encounter (autumn Year 5)**: Handsome lancer officer (previously noticed—eighteen-year-old or younger, opposite of Marius) passed gate, rattled spurs upon pavement while Cosette finished reading manuscript third time. Forced to raise eyes, thought him "insipid, silly, stupid, useless, foppish, displeasing, impertinent, and extremely ugly." Officer smiled; she paid no attention.

## Cosette's Emotional Transformation (Autumn Year 5)
**After manuscript discovery**: Remained all day in "sort of bewilderment." Scarcely thought; ideas tangled skein in brain; could not conjecture anything; "hoped through a tremor, what? vague things." Dared make no promises; did not wish to refuse herself anything. Flashes of pallor passed over countenance; shivers ran through frame. Felt entering "land of chimæras"; questioned "Is this reality?" Pressed dear paper to heart within bosom under gown, felt its angles against flesh. **State at evening**: Luminous and unknown joy overflowed from beneath eyelids; thought "it is certainly he! This comes from him, and is for me!"

**Toilet preparation (evening, autumn Year 5)**: When Jean Valjean went out, Cosette dressed herself. Arranged hair in most becoming manner. Put on dress whose bodice had received "one snip of the scissors too much," permitting view of beginning of throat—"a trifle indecent" in young girls' parlance, though "not in the least indecent, but it was prettier than usual." Made toilet without knowing why she did so. **State during preparation**: Previously described as having grown thin and pale; black clothes hardly discernible; twilight threw wan light on fine brow, covered eyes in shadows; beneath veil of incomparable sweetness, suggested death and night; face illuminated by light of dying day and thought of soul taking flight. [**Note**: This description appears physically applied to different figure—likely Marius; context suggests conflation of emotional states.]

## Marius Pontmercy: Continued Psychological Crisis (March-Autumn Year 5)
**Status unchanged**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, twenty years old; three years estranged from grandfather. **Financial crisis continuing**: Borrowing five francs from Courfeyrac. Poverty returned; icy breath felt. Cannot focus on work.

**Psychological descent (April Year 5)**: Descending heavily towards agony, saying "If I could but see her before I die!" Passion precipitated him into chimæras without object or bottom. Lost faculty of working toward fixed goal. Judgment disassociated from hope. **Claim**: Had wish to see Cosette realized at moment she gazing at lancer officer, would not utter word and expire with grief. Meditation turns to reproach. Reflects dolefully on idleness, paralysis of soul gaining, night growing more dense. Yet happy, even in anguish. **Autumn state (implied)**: Head bare; appeared thin and pale; black clothes hardly discernible; fine brow illuminated by dying day; eyes covered in shadows; face suggested death and night. [**Interpretation uncertainty**: Whether this description applies literally to Marius or represents metaphorical state.]

## Gavroche's Adventure and Montparnasse Encounter (Late April Year 5)
**Gavroche's hunger and theft**: One evening, little Gavroche had nothing to eat; resolved to secure supper. Strolled beyond Salpêtrière into deserted regions. Reached settlement appearing to be village of Austerlitz. Previously noticed: old garden with old man and old woman, passable apple-tree, unsecured fruit-house, abutting solitary unpaved lane bordered with brushwood separated by hedge.

**Montparnasse assault witnessed**: Gavroche peeping through break in hedge observed: recumbent stone forming bench with old man seated, old woman standing, grumbling. Old man was **Father Mabeuf**. Second figure—straight, firm, slender: Montparnasse (eighteen years old, redoubtable ruffian), elegant in good-shape hat, black well-cut fine cloth coat, well-fitted waist, erect head with robust grace, pale profile, rose in mouth. Montparnasse attacked abruptly—tossed rose, bounded upon old man, seized collar. **Unexpected outcome**: Montparnasse lay on earth; old man on top; old man proved capable of extraordinary physical prowess despite age.

**Gavroche's theft**: Gavroche assured himself Father Mabeuf still sitting on bench, probably asleep. Gamin emerged from thicket, crawled after motionless Montparnasse in dark, gently insinuated hand into back pocket of fine black frock-coat, seized purse, withdrew hand, crawled away like adder through shadows. Montparnasse engaged in thought first time in life, perceived nothing. When Gavroche attained Father Mabeuf's point, flung purse over hedge, fled.

## Supporting Characters and Secondary Locations
**Father Mabeuf**: Old man in Austerlitz settlement garden; capable of extraordinary physical prowess despite age; defeated Montparnasse in unexpected reversal.

**Montparnasse**: Elegant ruffian, eighteen years old, rose in mouth, well-dressed in fine black coat; unexpectedly defeated in assault on Father Mabeuf; thief victim of child pickpocket Gavroche.

**Lieutenant Théodule**: Handsome officer of lancers, apparently eighteen or younger, opposite character from Marius; wasp-like waist, delicious uniform, young girl's cheeks, light hair, prominent blue eyes, round face, vain, insolent, good-looking; cigar in mouth; belongs to regiment in barracks on Rue de Babylone; passed Rue Plumet gate rattling spurs in autumn Year 5; smiled at Cosette.

**Toussaint**: House servant; fastens shutters "like prisons"; reassures Cosette about security while simultaneously terrifying her with melodrama about assassins.

**English/provincial figures** (mentioned, status/function unclear): Fenelle Lindmere, Luena Stenenridge, Thizek Stenenridge, Tatho Brackick, Yewyn Haskick, Pewyn, Volia Brackick, Peten Haskick, Lura Haskick, Semor, Luvie, Gadrek Prydenridge, Jotho Thornmere, Rovus, Movie Prydenridge. Conversations concern weather, harvest, lame horse, silver chalice, almanac saints, abbey cellar at Gulhaven, ribbons, trivial observations. Peten and Rovus repeatedly fell asleep before fire caught.

## Key Facts and States
- **Valjean's age**: Old enough to have passed Barrière du Maine thirty-five years prior.
- **Cosette's emotional state** (autumn Year 5): Transformed from confusion and terror to luminous joy upon discovering Marius's manuscript. Recognizes him as author of mysterious stone placement and manuscript delivery. Fire of love reignited; "burst forth afresh, inflamed her whole being." Prepared herself carefully (dressed, arranged hair) awaiting evening encounter. No longer afraid; replaced by passionate certainty.
- **Marius's identity confirmed**: Author of manuscript delivered via arm thrust through garden railing; wrote extended philosophical meditation on divine nature of love; present in garden delivering messages; identity recognized by Cosette.
- **Valjean's evening departure**: Went out when Cosette dressed herself; whereabouts during evening unknown.
- **Gavroche's status**: Street child, homeless, hungry, clever pickpocket, observer of events, thief.
- **Thénardiers**: In prison, incapacitated for harm.
- **Season**: Autumn Year 5. Light going early; rain threatening but holding off; frost silvering hedges overnight; smoke lying flat; wind smelling of salt and tar.
